claim: asm.mp3 is handed to native code as (FileDescriptor, startOffset, length) from AssetManager.openFd
observation: assetManager.openFd("asm.mp3"); start=(int)getStartOffset(); length=(int)getLength(); JNIDatInit(getFileDescriptor(), start, length)
interpretation: The archive is read through the APK file descriptor at a byte offset; offsets are truncated to Java int (32-bit).

claim: JNIDatInit obtains the fd, dups it and opens a FILE* in binary mode; records start/length in globals
observation: env slots +0x18 FindClass("java/io/FileDescriptor"), +0x54 NewGlobalRef, +0x178 GetFieldID("descriptor","I"), +0x190 GetIntField; bl PLT dup; stores: gJavaAssetStart(0x9102c)=r3 arg, gJavaAssetLength(0x91030)=5th arg [sp+0x128], gJavaAssetFid(0x91028)=dup result; fdopen(fd,"rb") -> gDatFP(0x91024); fid==0 or fd object==NULL -> wprintf + return; fdopen NULL -> wprintf("***ERROR*** gDatFP==0") + return
interpretation: gJavaAssetFid holds the dup'd descriptor (name notwithstanding). No error is reported to Java.

claim: Directory size is the u32 at archive offset 8, read from a 244-byte probe
observation: fseek(fp,start,SEEK_SET); gDat=0; fread(sp+0xc,1,0xf4,fp); ldr r3,[sp,#0x14] (= probe+8); RShellMemoryMalloc(r3,"NOT GIVEN")
interpretation: dir_size = u32@8, which is also record 0's data_offset field; the fread result is not checked (short archive -> uninitialised stack bytes). For the real archive dir_size = 34701 = 0x878d.

claim: RShellMemoryMalloc(int,char*) is a tail call to malloc (label argument ignored)
observation: b PLT:malloc
interpretation: Allocation size is the only semantic.

claim: The whole directory block [0, dir_size) is loaded into gDat
observation: fseek(fp,start,SEEK_SET); fread(gDat,1,dir_size,fp)
interpretation: gDat (0x10144c) holds an image of archive bytes [0,dir_size) (then patched in place, EV-ASSET-0006). fread result unchecked.

claim: count = s32 at gDat+0; record i at gDat+4+24*i; its first word (name offset) is rewritten IN PLACE to the pointer gDat+name_offset
observation: ldr r1,[r3] (count) -> cRHash::Init; loop: ip=gDat+(3i<<3); ldr r1,[ip,#4]; add r1,gDat,r1; str r1,[ip,#4]; bl cRHash::Add(hash, r1, i); cmp count,i; bgt (signed)
interpretation: Name offsets are relative to the first archive byte (= fd start offset), i.e. the same origin as the directory. ARM64 hazard: a 32-bit pointer stored into a 32-bit on-disk field; the reconstruction keeps fields as uint32_t and host pointers separately.

claim: The directory name index is built with cRHash::Init(&gDatHash, count, DatHashGetString) then Add(name_i, i) for i=0..count-1 in order
observation: r0=gDatHash (0x101494, symbol size 2060), r1=count, r2=DatHashGetString (0x19954); Add(r0=hash, r1=name ptr, r2=i)
interpretation: Hash values are record indices; insertion order = index order.

claim: DatHashGetString(i) returns the fixed-up name pointer of record i
interpretation: Search compares against directory strings; no bounds check on i.

claim: RShellDatFind(name) returns a pointer to record i (gDat+4+24*i) or NULL
observation: gDat==0 -> 0; i=cRHash::Search(&gDatHash,name); i==-1 -> 0; else gDat + (3i<<3) + 4
interpretation: Lookup takes the name verbatim (no path normalisation, no directory prefix). Confirmed by execution (tests/differential/assets, suite jnidatinit).

claim: Record field layout: +0 name_offset, +4 data_offset, +8 decoded_size, +12 stored_size, +16 codec, +20 u16 width, +22 u16 height
observation: *outSize=[rec+8]; buf==-1 -> return [rec+4]; buf==NULL -> malloc([rec+8]); ldmib rec,{r1,r2,r3} (=+4,+8,+12); [sp]=[rec+0x10]; [sp+4]=ldrh [rec+0x14]; [sp+8]=ldrh [rec+0x16]; PfmLoadFileDat(buf, off, dec, stored, codec, w, h)
interpretation: Field meanings follow from PfmLoadFileDat's use of each parameter (EV-ASSET-0017). Names 'decoded_size'/'stored_size' are interpretations of that use.

claim: cRHash::Calc(s) = (sum over bytes of (byte | 0x20)) & 0xff; bytes loaded with LDRB (zero-extended); empty string -> 0
observation: ldrb r3,[r1]; beq ret0; loop: orr r2,r3,#0x20; ldrb r3,[r1,#1]!; add r0,r0,r2; bne; and r0,r0,#0xff
interpretation: 256 buckets. Hash is case-insensitive for letters but also merges e.g. '@'/'`'. Differential: 6,424 inputs incl. all bytes 0x01-0xff and a 16.8 MB string (32-bit wrap), 0 mismatches.

claim: Plain-char signedness cannot affect cRHash::Calc's result
observation: The original uses LDRB. A reconstruction mutated to sign-extend bytes produced 0 mismatches over 17,894 comparisons.
interpretation: Only bits 0-7 of each term reach the result (sum mod 256), and sign extension only changes bits 8-31; the comparison routine also only tests byte equality / a-z range. So char signedness is unobservable here; the reconstruction still uses unsigned char to mirror LDRB.

claim: cRHash object layout: 256 x {int32 value (-1 empty), node* next} at +0x000; +0x800 node pool; +0x804 next free node; +0x808 char*(*)(int) getter
observation: str r2,[r4,#0x808]; loop off=0..0x7f8 step 8: [off]=-1,[off+4]=0; pool=malloc(count<<3) -> [0x800]; memset(pool,0,count<<3); [0x804]=[0x800]
interpretation: Total 0x80c = 2060 bytes = size of gDatHash symbol. No malloc NULL check; count<<3 computed in 32 bits.

claim: cRHash::Add appends at the chain tail; empty-head test is value == -1; no duplicate detection; no pool bound check
observation: b=Calc; if [this+8b]==-1 store value in head; else walk ->next to last; last->next=[0x804]; *[0x804]=value; [0x804]+=8
interpretation: Chains are in insertion order. Adding value -1 to an empty head leaves it empty. Chain structure of the original matched the reconstruction exactly (differential suites table/jnidatinit).

claim: cRHash::Search returns the value of the FIRST chain entry whose name equals the key case-insensitively (ASCII a-z only), else -1
observation: b=Calc(key); head==-1 -> -1; per node: cand=getter(value) via ldr pc,[r4,#0x808]; per byte: equal if c1==c2 or fold(c1)==fold(c2), fold(c)=(u8)(c-0x61)<=0x19 ? c-0x20 : c; lengths must match; miss -> next; end -> mvn r0,#0
interpretation: No path normalisation, no extension handling. First-added wins for duplicate names.

claim: cRHash::UnInit only frees the pool
observation: ldr r0,[r0,#0x800]; b free
interpretation: Bucket heads keep stale values; the reconstruction resets them.

claim: PfmLoadFileDat dispatches on codec: 0 raw fread of decoded_size bytes; 1 zip via JAVAC_UnZip; 2 JPEG via JAVAC_UnJpg; 3 PNG via JAVAC_UnPng; >3 nothing
observation: gDatFP==0 -> wprintf("ERROR: Cannot open File"); cmp codec,#3; addls pc,pc,codec<<2. case0: fseek(fp,off+gJavaAssetStart); fread(dst,1,dec). case1: tmp=malloc(stored); fseek; fread(tmp,1,stored); JAVAC_UnZip(dst,dec,tmp,stored); free. case2/3: tmp=malloc(stored); ...; JAVAC_UnJpg/UnPng(dst+0x12,dec,tmp,stored,w,h); write TGA header; free
interpretation: Established by instructions and by executing the original loader on every reachable real record and on a synthetic raw record with decoded_size(2) < stored_size(5): the original read exactly 2 bytes (mutation m5).

claim: Data offsets are relative to the archive's first byte (gJavaAssetStart is added before fseek)
observation: ldr r1,[gJavaAssetStart]; add r1,sl(data_offset),r1; fseek(fp,r1,SEEK_SET)
interpretation: Same origin as the directory and name offsets. The sum is 32-bit (long on ARM32): ARM64 port should compute file offsets in 64-bit. Differential used a start offset of 0x1235 behind a fake fd.

claim: codec 1 payloads are decoded by Java JAVAUnZip(byte[] out(decoded_size), byte[] in(stored bytes)) which copies the FIRST ZipInputStream entry into out
location: v7a:0x14b60-0x14c60; gJAVAFunction table v7a:0x8b3f0 entry 14 (+0xa8) = JAVAUnZip ([B[B)V; ADRenderer.java:234-260
observation: NewByteArray(dec)->out, NewByteArray(stored)->in, SetByteArrayRegion(in,0,stored,tmp), CallVoidMethod(gJavaObj, mid14, out, in), GetByteArrayRegion(out,0,dec,dst)
interpretation: Java copies decoded bytes until EOF; bytes past out.length throw (caught, message only), shorter output leaves zeros in out.

claim: JAVAC_UnPng/JAVAC_UnJpg place bitmap rows bottom-up: row_bytes = decoded_size / height (signed), Java row r -> dst + (height-1-r)*row_bytes
location: v7a:0x1457c-0x145e0 (UnPng; UnJpg v7a:0x149e8 same shape, method entry 15 +0xb4 / UnPng entry 16 +0xc0)
observation: bl __aeabi_idiv(outSize,h) BEFORE the h>0 test; loop: GetByteArrayRegion(out, r*rb, rb, dst+rb*(h-1) - r*rb)
interpretation: Vertical flip into TGA bottom-left order. height 0 divides by zero. Confirmed by execution with a synthetic aperiodic pixel pattern (mutation m4 detected).

claim: For JPEG/PNG the loader writes an 18-byte TGA header: type 2, width, height, 32 bpp, descriptor 8
observation: strb 0 at +0,+1,+3..+7; strh 0 at +8,+0xa; strb 2 at +2; strh w at +0xc; strh h at +0xe; strb 0x20 at +0x10; strb 8 at +0x11
interpretation: Decoded images become in-memory TGA images, the same representation as the zipped .TGA files. Confirmed by execution (mutation m6 detected).

claim: RShellLoadFile: buf==(void*)-1 returns data_offset; buf==NULL allocates decoded_size bytes; *size=decoded_size; missing name falls back to a real file
location: v7a:0x1b980-0x1bae8; overload RShellLoadFile(char*,int*) v7a:0x1baec = (name, NULL, size)
observation: cmn r7,#1 -> ldr r7,[r5,#4]; r7==0 -> RShellMemoryMalloc([rec+8]); miss -> wprintf("FileMissing from gDat %s"), RShellConvertFileName ('/'->'_', A-Z->a-z), PfmLoadFile -> JAVACFindFile/JAVACLoadFile
interpretation: For images the loader writes 18 + (dec/h)*h bytes; with the observed dec = w*h*4+19 that fits in a decoded_size allocation. Confirmed by execution (LoadFile(-1) and *size for all reachable records).

claim: Observed archive structure: 734 records; dir_size 34701; names packed in record order right after the table (0x44d4..0x878d); data regions contiguous in record order from 34701 to EOF; no gaps, overlaps or trailing bytes
observation: tools/extraction/asm_archive.py layout analysis
interpretation: Counts are observations of this file, not format constants.

claim: Observed codecs: raw 636 (272 text, 364 unknown binary .SMO), zip 70, jpeg 11, png 17; all zip payloads are complete one-entry deflate archives whose decoded length equals decoded_size and CRC matches; PNG IHDR / JPEG SOF dims equal record dims; decoded_size = w*h*4 + 19 for all 28 images
observation: magic-based sniffing and zip decoding in tools/extraction/asm_archive.py
interpretation: The '+19' is 18 (TGA header) + 1; the extra byte's purpose is a hypothesis (rounding slack).

claim: Zipped TGA records carry their image dims in the dims field (66/66 match the TGA header) although PfmLoadFileDat ignores dims for codec 1; non-image zips have dims 0
location: archive records with codec 1; v7a:0x14dbc-0x14e1c (case 1 does not use w/h)
observation: manifest decoded.sniff vs interpreted.dims
interpretation: dims is informational for codec 1 (hypothesis: written by the build tool for every image).

claim: Record 54 'SPRITES/MOUSE.TGA' duplicates record 43's name (different bytes); by-name lookup returns 43, so record 54 is unreachable
observation: Original JNIDatInit+RShellDatFind executed in Unicorn returned index 43 for the name; the reconstruction agrees.
interpretation: Extractor keeps both, marks 54 'shadowed' and writes it to a de-duplicated path.

claim: The scrambled-.dat path (RShellDatInit -> RShellLoadFileHeader -> RShellUnScrambleDat) is dead code on Android; asm.mp3 is not scrambled
observation: No BL to 0x1c018 or 0x1bc38 in .text; the only words equal to those addresses are symbol-table values. JNIDatInit and PfmLoadFileDat contain no call to RShellUnScrambleDat.
interpretation: The Android build reads the archive raw. (RShellLoadFileHeader's own compare folds only the key, i.e. expects upper-case names.)

claim: JNIDatUnInit does nothing observable; the archive stays open for the process lifetime
observation: JNIDatUnInit = two wprintf calls; wprintf = push {r0-r3}; add sp,#16; bx lr (no-op). RShellUnInit (fclose(gDatFP); gDat=0) has no BL callers.
interpretation: Java onStop calls JNIDatUnInit (SnailMailActivity.java:109); gDat/gDatHash/gDatFP are never released. JNIDatInit also calls DeleteLocalRef on a global ref (v7a:0x1542c-0x1543c).

claim: Loaded images are uploaded as textures from the TGA representation
observation: reads u16 tga+0xc (w), u16 tga+0xe (h), byte tga+0x10 (bpp): 0x20 -> glTexImage2D(GL_TEXTURE_2D,0,GL_RGBA,w,h,0,GL_RGBA,GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE,tga+0x12); 0x18 -> GL_RGB
interpretation: Partial: other consumers (objects/.SMO, levels, fonts) not analysed here.

claim: v5 cRHash::Calc has the same instruction sequence as v7a
observation: identical 12 instructions to v7a:0x7d114
interpretation: Other v5 asset functions are NOT re-verified.

claim: Zip entry names inside codec-1 payloads equal RShellConvertFileName(record name)
observation: entry_name == name with '/'->'_' and A-Z->a-z for all 70
interpretation: Hypothesis: the archive builder zipped files from a flattened lower-case tree; not used by the runtime (JAVAUnZip ignores entry names).

claim: Reconstructed sm_rhash_* and sm_asm_directory_* agree exactly with the original ARM32 code on all tested inputs
observation: 17,894 exact comparisons, 0 mismatches (calc, table, jnidatinit+loader on the real archive and on the synthetic fixture). Mutations m2-m6 of the reconstruction are each detected; m1 (signedness) is output-invariant (EV-ASSET-0012).
interpretation: REFERENCE_VALIDATED for the tested inputs only. Java decoding (BitmapFactory) is replaced by stand-ins and is NOT validated.
